Date: 2026-12-02 | Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Starlight Head of ML), Carlos Rivera (Starlight Platform), Dr. Emily Park (Starlight CTO), Nina Patel (Starlight Privacy)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on unit economics: tokens/sec/$, caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed last week's benchmark, discussed discrepancy in per-token costs due to cache hit rates and batching parameters, agreed on next benchmarks and action items including 1M token run, updated cost spreadsheet, and exec review for pricing.
topics: Benchmark review: discrepancy in tokens/sec and cost vs expected
Batching tradeoffs: latency p50/p95 vs throughput
Quantization/instance types and reserved capacity options
Security/compliance notes and audit log requirements
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — quick roll call. priya, you here?
[00:05] Priya: yep, here. Liam on my left.
[00:08] Maya: hi all, maya here. Carlos and emily on our side.
[00:12] Jordan: great. agenda is cost econ, benchmark results, caching/batching tuning and next steps. we had the staging run last week so want to dig into the numbers.

[02:00] Priya: quick recap — last week's 100k-token run reported ~420 tokens/sec on our rtx-like instances with the current config, cost came out higher than expected ~0.018 tokens per token-dollar unit, um, basically tokens/$ math looked off because cache hit rate in staging was low.
[02:25] Carlos: yeah i saw that, our KV cash — cash spelled C-A-S-H in the logs — was only about 12% hit, which surprised us. in prod we expect more prefix reuse but staging traffic was too random.
[03:10] Maya: right the chat sessions in staging used test prompts with lots of unique user context so we didn't get representative cache hits.

[05:00] Priya: ok so breakdown — two levers: batching and cache. batching gives throughput gains (tokens/sec up) but increases per-request latency at p95; cache reduces model compute per token and thus tokens/$ dramatically.
[05:22] Jordan: can you quantify? like if cache hit rate goes from 12% to 60% what numbers change?
[05:35] Priya: yes. ballpark from our bench: with current quant profile and instance, baseline (no cache, small batch) = 420 tokens/sec, cost A = $X per 1M tokens — i'll send exact sheet. with 60% prefix/KV hit, effective model compute drops so tokens/sec effective increases to ~620-700 depending on how much decoding is short-circuited, and tokens/$ improves by roughly 35-45%.
[06:10] Emily: that's significant. how sensitive is that to sequence length? our average conversation prefix is 180 tokens.
[06:25] Priya: shorter prefixes yield higher hit reuse; if your prefixes are consistent across calls (templates, system prompts) cache effect is bigger. with 180 token prefix we still see 30-40% savings at 50% hit rate.

[08:00] Carlos: regarding batching — we tried batch size 8 in staging, latency p50 was fine but p95 spiked to ~1.4s which is near our app threshold. can we get smaller latency with the same throughput?
[08:20] Priya: tradeoff— continuous batching in Redwood groups requests over a small wait window (we used 20ms). increasing batch size helps throughput but increases queuing. options: tune the batch window, dynamic batching based on SLA, or use dedicated pool with higher concurrency to keep latency low while batching. Also quantization profile (int8 vs int4) impacts CPU/GPU kernel throughput.
[09:00] Jordan: so product-wise we can route latency-sensitive routes to dedicated low-batch pools and background/rate-limited routes to high-batch pools to optimize $/token.

[11:00] Maya: curious about quantization — we tested int8 yesterday, saw lower latency but some diffs in hallucination/quality. any guidance?
[11:20] Priya: yes, int8 usually preserves quality for many LLMs but depends on model. Redwood Optimize suggests model-specific quant profiles; we can run a quick eval on your safety/regression suite to measure any quality deltas. for now, conservative: int8 on non-critical routes, float16 for critical scoring.

[13:30] Carlos: on reserved capacity — if we commit to a monthly pool, what's the unit economics? does tokens/$ drop linearly or is there a step change?
[13:50] Jordan: reserved gives step discounts on instance-hour costs and priority on capacity. effective tokens/$ improves ~15-35% depending on commit size and whether you use autoscaling bursts. we'll include scenario tables in the pricing doc.

[15:30] Priya: back to the benchmark discrepancy — i dug into the logs, saw that KV miss penalty and cache replication delays added ~8% overhead to the run; staging had a single node cache config, whereas our recommended setup is a distributed cache with local hot shards. that reduces miss penalty.
[16:10] Maya: can you provide config? Carlos will flip settings in staging.
[16:18] Priya: yes i'll export the cache config and suggested TTLs. expectation: TTLs for prefix entries ~12h for sessions, and max shard size small to keep local hit rate high.

[18:00] Emily: security question — what's logged for cache hits? our privacy team worries about PII and retention.
[18:18] Jordan: Redwood's cache stores KV ids and tokenized prefixes, not raw user PII in plaintext; plus we support KMS encryption and customer-managed keys for private deployments. Nina, anything from privacy side?
[18:36] Nina: need to see data flow diagram and audit log retention policy; also confirm that we can purge cache entries on demand.
[18:50] Jordan: noted, we'll attach the security brief and the cache purge API docs.

[20:30] Carlos: one thing we noticed — the profiling shows hot spots in the attention kernel when sequence length spikes above 1k. our median is 250 but we have bursts to 1.2k. how does that affect tokens/$?
[20:50] Priya: long sequences increase per-token compute non-linearly; if bursts are rare, cost amortization is small, but if bursts are common you might want sequence-length truncation policies, summarization, or a specialized long-context config. Also different kernels/compilers behave differently; we'll recommend model variant or chunking.

[23:00] Maya: for the 1M token run we plan to simulate traffic with realistic prefix reuse and sequence distribution; do you have a script?
[23:12] Jordan: yes we have a workload generator template. i'll share it. make sure to enable prefix caching in your staging and run with both batch window 20ms and 40ms to compare.

[25:00] Priya: i want to call out an important nuance: tokens/sec metric is useful but tokens/sec per dollar (tokens/$) is the ultimate operational metric. small changes to cache hit (e.g., 10% delta) can swing tokens/$ materially. we'll provide a sensitivity table.

[27:30] Carlos: about routing — if we split routes by SLA, how complex is the configuration?
[27:40] Jordan: Redwood Console supports per-route policies; you can set model, pool, batch window, and fallback policies. it's declarative yaml or via UI. we'll share an example.

[29:00] Emily: what's the timeline if we want to pilot reserved capacity after the POC? can we spin up a dedicated pool in 2-3 weeks?
[29:12] Jordan: yes typical lead is 2 weeks for dedicated pool in same region; enterprise onboarding and contracts add time. for a small pilot we can often provision within a week if capacity available.

[31:00] Priya: any other blockers from your side that affect cost? e.g., rate limiting, burst patterns, or model mix?
[31:12] Maya: model mix — we use a heavy reranker for search which is expensive per token. looking at possibly moving that to a smaller model + rerank by embeddings. that could shift tokens/$ significantly.
[31:40] Priya: embeddings + light rerank is often cheaper and more predictable; we'll include a hybrid suggestion in the doc.

[33:00] Carlos: some of our calls had garbled speaker tags in the logs; not sure if that affected batching analysis.
[33:08] Priya: that could cause uneven batching since speaker attribution sometimes used to group sessions. we'll provide log parsing guidance.

[35:00] Maya: ok let's recap next steps — send cost sheet, run benchmark, cache config, exec review.
[35:12] Jordan: yep that's the plan. Priya will own the cost sheet.

[36:30] Priya: quick note on metrics to capture in the 1M run: total tokens, tokens/sec (mean), tokens/sec (p50/p95), tokens/$ effective, cache hit rate, average sequence length, p50/p95 latency. also model flop counts if available.

[38:00] Carlos: is there a recommended sampling interval for telemetry? we saw spikes that the 60s aggregate missed.
[38:10] Priya: 10s resolution during benchmark is ideal, with detailed traces sampled at 1% for p95 investigation.

[40:00] Nina: for compliance we need audit log retention of 90 days and SSO integration, SAML works?
[40:10] Jordan: yes SAML SSO is supported, audit logs can be exported and retention extended as an add-on. we'll include that in the security packet.

[42:00] Maya: any red flags on cost direction? we want to make sure no surprise regressions after rollouts.
[42:12] Priya: main risks are cache hit lower than expected and unbounded sequence-length growth. both manageable: we can do guardrails (TTL, truncation policies) and monitor via regressions alerts.

[44:00] Jordan: final— we'll share updated cost spreadsheet and config by Monday 2026-12-06, staging 1M run by 12/09, and schedule exec pricing review for week of 12/13.
[44:25] Maya: sounds good. thanks all.
[44:30] Emily: thanks.
[44:35] Carlos: thanks.
[44:40] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links. meeting adjourned.
